summary: Snohomish County, WA L-4 cab built 1935 and ended in 1964; sources disagree on removed vs destroyed and on whether four foundation corners remain.

facts.status_note: Register says removed in 1964; Firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts say destroyed; WillhiteWeb says burned down; a 2017 visit saw nothing, while WillhiteWeb describes foundations

staffing.status: manned lookout in 1956; a ranger stationed at the guard station could hike up to staff it during high fire danger or lightning storms (WillhiteWeb); no later staffing found

access.note: Parking area off the Mountain Loop Highway near the old guard station; a one-mile trail with two forks leads to the site (Register visit report)

visit.trail_note: One mile (Register visit report) or 1.2 miles (WillhiteWeb) from the parking area; take the right-hand fork at each junction

events.note: Panorama photos taken July 30, 1935; WillhiteWeb says on the roof
Activated March 20, 1942 and deactivated October 16, 1943 at the Seattle Filter Center; WillhiteWeb says the AWS used it for aircraft spotting in 1942
Visitor recalls a manned lookout when first visiting in 1956
Firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts say destroyed in 1964
WillhiteWeb says the lookout was burned down in 1964
Registered January 26, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek
June 7, 2017 visit report: nothing remains; trees block the view

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says removed in 1964; Firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts say destroyed; WillhiteWeb says burned down. All agree on 1964, so the story reports all three words.
A 2017 Register visit report says nothing remains; WillhiteWeb's 2014 photos describe four corner foundations. The story reports both and does not settle it.
WillhiteWeb calls the site Barlow Point; the Register and Forest Lookouts use Barlow Pass. The story uses Barlow Pass, the registry name.
Register visit report says a one-mile trail; WillhiteWeb says 1.2 miles.

sources.title: Barlow Pass Lookout Site - Guard Station

notes_for_editor: The cab is gone but the sources disagree on how it ended (removed, destroyed or burned, all in 1964) and on whether foundations remain (2017 visit says nothing; WillhiteWeb's 2014 photo captions describe four corner foundations). The brief's name is Barlow Pass; WillhiteWeb uses Barlow Point. Trail length differs (one mile vs 1.2 miles). Access is marked public from the visit report's signed parking and trail description. facts.height_m was left out. Used 0 WebSearches and 4 page reads, plus one checked grep.
